competences: The learner recalls the road-transport, sign and traffic-light content of the week.
The learner identifies safe road-use actions from the week’s notes.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and writes: road, sign, traffic, lights, safe, footpath.
objectives: By the end of the review, learners should be able to name road-transport means and identify familiar road signs.
By the end of the review, learners should be able to state safe ways of using the road.
priorKnowledge: The review brings together the four preceding lessons on road transport, signs, traffic lights and safe road use.
materials: Road-transport and road-sign charts used during the week
Traffic-light colour and meaning cards used in the preceding lessons
references: P I Literacy Lesson Notes Term III

steps.content: Transport pictures and the starter question: Write four means of road transport.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays road-transport and road-sign charts used during the week and asks: "Write four means of road transport." Learners first identify familiar pictures; the teacher connects their responses to week 2 review.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners look at the transport pictures, identify familiar words, and give oral responses to the starter question before copying any notes.

steps.content: Summary: road transport: Road transport moves people and goods on land. Buses, cars, lorries and bicycles use roads.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Road transport moves people and goods on land. Buses, cars, lorries and bicycles use roads. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write four means of road transport." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for summary: road transport, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Summary: road signs: Road signs guide road users. A zebra crossing is a safe place to cross a road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Road signs guide road users. A zebra crossing is a safe place to cross a road. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for summary: road signs, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Summary: traffic lights: Red means stop; orange means get ready; green means go.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Red means stop; orange means get ready; green means go. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for summary: traffic lights, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Summary: safe road use: Obey traffic rules. Look right, left and right again before crossing. Use footpaths. Do not run while crossing a road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Obey traffic rules. Look right, left and right again before crossing. Use footpaths. Do not run while crossing a road. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for summary: safe road use, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: 1. Write four means of road transport. 2. Write any one importance of road signs to road users. 3. Name the three colours of the traffic lights. 4. Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green. 5. Write down any two good ways of using the road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise: "Write four means of road transport." "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." "Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green." "Write down any two good ways of using the road." The teacher reads each item clearly, checks individual answers, and uses the transport chart to correct mistaken identifications.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions in their books, complete any specified matching or drawing, and correct their responses with the teacher.

source.quote: Write four means of road transport

A zebra crossing is a safe place to cross a road.; Red means stop; orange means get ready; green means go.; Obey traffic rules. Look right, left and right again before crossing. Use footpaths. Do not run while crossing a road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks the lesson objectives using these exercise items: "Write four means of road transport." "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." The teacher confirms correct answers against the board notes and identifies learners needing further picture-supported practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give short oral answers, compare them with the transport pictures and board notes, and correct any remaining errors in their books.

assessment: Check the written exercise and oral responses: Write four means of road transport. Write any one importance of road signs to road users. Name the three colours of the traffic lights. Mark against the source-based answers and revisit incorrect identifications using the transport chart.
homework: Complete or correct this sourced exercise item in your book: Write down any two good ways of using the road.
